item.title: ByteDance's Seedance 2.0 Video Generation Model Launches
item.description:
ByteDance’s Seedance 2.0 Video Generation Model Launches

ByteDance’s Seedance 2.0, the industry’s first model supporting simultaneous quad-modal input — image, video, audio, and text, has launched. This innovative tool offers a range of features and capabilities for video generation.

🔍 Overview

  • Seedance 2.0 is a video generation model developed by ByteDance.
  • It supports simultaneous quad-modal input — image, video, audio, and text.
  • The model can generate videos up to 1080p resolution and 4–15 seconds duration.

🧩 How it works

  • Text-to-Video — Generate videos from text descriptions
  • Image-to-Video — Animate static images into dynamic videos
  • Video-to-Video — Transform and extend existing videos
  • Audio-Driven — Generate videos driven by audio input

⚙️ Key details

  • Auto dubbing & scoring — Automatic voiceover and background music
  • A curated collection of high-quality video generation prompts is available, including Seedance API guides, character consistency tips, and advanced video workflows.

🚀 Availability

  • The curated collection of video generation prompts is available for educational purposes.

💡 Why it matters

  • Seedance 2.0 offers a unique and innovative approach to video generation, with a wide range of features and capabilities.
  • The model’s support for simultaneous quad-modal input sets it apart from other video generation tools.
  • The curated collection of video generation prompts provides users with a valuable resource for creating high-quality videos.

#Seedance2.0 #VideoGeneration #ByteDance #AI #QuadModalInput

Source: YouMind-OpenLab/awesome-seedance-2-prompts

item.title: MiniMax H3 Director: New ComfyUI Node for Multi-Clip Video Generation
item.description:
MiniMax H3 Director: New ComfyUI Node for Multi-Clip Video Generation

MiniMax H3 Director is a new ComfyUI node designed for long video and multi-segment generation. It integrates segment planning, conditional encoding, sampling, decoding, and export into a single interface, utilizing the official MiniMax H3 Image-to-Video and Reference-to-Video models alongside KSampler and AV separation decoding pipelines. The node natively outputs stereo audio.

🧩 How it works

The node manages a visual timeline for video generation, supporting several task types and advanced control over segmentation and transitions.

  • Segmentation and Editing: Users can upload video within the node to split, equally divide, or intelligently segment scenes using PySceneDetect. Split points are selectable and deletable, with a visual timeline previewing each segment’s range and thumbnail.
  • Grouped Keyframes: An independent first-last frame timeline allows multiple keyframe groups. Users can either write prompts for text-to-video or upload first/last frames (officially supporting last-frame-only uploads).
  • Inter-Segment Guidance: When enabled, empty groups use the last N frames of the previous segment for motion and audio continuity. Users can adjust duration via dragging and select specific groups to run.
  • Prompt Syntax: Prompts utilize <Picture N>, <Video K>, or <Audio J> tags (or @ references). The timeline preview and selection states remain synchronized with the prompts.
  • Reference Binding: For style-source video timelines, each segment’s source frame is automatically bound to <Video 1>. For reference-to-video tasks, additional reference images (up to 9) and audio (up to 3) can be attached per group.
  • Selective Sampling: When enabled, only checked segments or material groups are sampled. Unchecked segments can be filled with cache or source frames during export.
  • Audio Integration: Audio is generated in the same sampling pass as the visuals. For video-to-video and reference-video tasks, users can choose to generate sound, use original audio, or remain silent.
  • Reference Audio Slots: Users can select existing videos or local audio/video files. Selected videos immediately extract the first audio track as FLAC, saved directly to the input/ directory.

⚙️ Key details

The node supports various task types and integrates external modules to refine the generation pipeline. A semantic bridge and self-lift module can be attached to specific ports; if unconnected, the system behaves as a standard single-stage one-sampling process. When connected, the self-lift module transforms the process into a low-resolution prefix, 3D lift, and high-resolution finish, using Euler sampling at the director canvas resolution.

External Modules and Refinement

Module/Feature Functionality
Semantic Bridge Uses a student MLP to rewrite official conditional tokens. Weights are not distributed with the plugin and must be placed in models/semantic_bridge/.
Self-Lift Connects to the selflift port. Enables a multi-stage sampling process (low-res prefix + 3D lift + high-res finish).
Refine Connects to the refine port. Offers three modes: refine (same-resolution refinement), upscale (upscale to target canvas then re-sample according to SIGMAS), and latent_upscale (upscale H3 latent only, no re-sampling).
Report Output Outputs the segment plan and per-segment task summary via the report port.

Model and Configuration Requirements

  • CLIP Loader: The type must be set to minimax (Qwen3-VL).
  • UNET Selection: t2v, i2v, and fl2v tasks use the fl2va UNET. r2v, v2v, and rv2v tasks use the ref2va UNET.
  • Distillation: The model is distilled from FL2VA. Note that r2v, v2v, and rv2v are forced compatibility modes, and caution is advised when using them.
  • ComfyUI Version: Users must upgrade ComfyUI to version 0.30.0 or higher.
  • Source Images: Outputting the original film to source_images fills the independent source_images output without altering the main images output.

🚀 Availability

The complete resource package, including MiniMax H3 model weights and example JSON workflows, is available via Comfyit Stirring Station · Article 506: “MiniMax H3 Models and Workflows.” After downloading, users must merge the models/ directory into ComfyUI/models/. The JSON workflow can be dragged directly into ComfyUI to begin use. The toolbar also supports importing and exporting director packages, which save timeline JSON and reference materials in a zip file.

#MiniMaxH3 #ComfyUI #VideoGeneration #AIVideo #ComfyNodes

Source: AIMixer/ComfyUI_MiniMaxH3_Director

item.title: Solar framework launches open tools for real-time video world models
item.description:
Solar framework launches open tools for real-time video world models

Solar is an open framework for interactive world models that spans open data, scalable training, long-horizon video generation, and real-time deployment. The repository contains code for two primary components: SolarWM and SolarRenderer.

🧩 How it works

The framework is built around two distinct modules that handle different aspects of video generation and rendering:

Component Function
SolarWM Enables real-time interaction, continuous exploration, and diverse generated worlds.
SolarRenderer Performs four-step, structure-conditioned video rendering with bidirectional and block-causal training and inference on MiniMax-H3.

⚙️ Key details

Several specific model releases and optimizations are included in the Solar framework:

  • SolarWM-H3 Memory: Improves long-term scene consistency and preserves visual details across revisits. Weights are available for the 33B model.
  • SolarWM-H3 Realtime: Enables low-latency interactive video generation from an image and a prompt, featuring real-time camera control.
  • H3 Streaming VAE Decoder: Allows for low-latency streaming video decoding that produces frames as latents arrive. It supports both the official MiniMax-H3 VAE and NVIDIA’s distilled StreamRender-H3 decoder.
  • Training Efficiency: Training for SolarWM-H3 is speeded up by 1.9–2.1× across Stage0.5, Stage1, and Stage2 with matching training trajectories, attributed to ResearchBoost-Agent.
  • Data: The SolarWM dataset and SolarRenderer dataset are hosted on Hugging Face.

🚀 Availability

  • Code: SolarWM and SolarRenderer code is available in the repository. Real-time deployment for SolarWM and the H3 Streaming VAE Decoder code are located in the deploy/solar_wm/ directory.
  • Weights: Model weights for both SolarWM and SolarRenderer are available on Hugging Face.
  • Demonstrations: An online demo for SolarRenderer is available on Hugging Face Spaces.
  • Documentation: Specific documentation for SolarWM is found in docs/solar_wm/ and for SolarRenderer in docs/solar_renderer/.

#SolarFramework #VideoGeneration #WorldModels #OpenSource #MiniMax-H3

Source: Junchao-cs/SolarWM

item.title: AVM Generates Video Streams Without Explicit 3D Representations
item.description:
AVM Generates Video Streams Without Explicit 3D Representations

Researchers have presented the Autoregressive View Model (AVM), a framework that generates scenes as a stream of views without constructing an explicit 3D representation.

🧩 How it works

AVM uses a unified in-context interface to condition on images or videos, generating short clips along a requested camera path. Visual context grounds reconstruction and interpolation, while a learned prior enables extrapolation into unseen regions.

⚙️ Key details

  • The model retrieves relevant views from inputs and generated history to form a bounded active context.
  • A pretrained bidirectional video diffusion transformer was fine-tuned with flow matching in an N-in-1-out formulation.
  • A causal model was subsequently tuned on its own rollouts to improve photorealism, reduce denoising steps, and limit long-horizon drift.
  • Training was scaled to approximately 8 million scenes and video clips.
  • Evaluation covers benchmarks for camera control, text control, visual quality, dynamics, sparse and 4D reconstruction, and long-horizon consistency.

💡 Why it matters

The results demonstrate that AVM adapts to diverse input and output settings through a single in-context interface. Additionally, the broader field is addressing variable-length data through frameworks like Variable Length Diffuse Everything (VL-DE), which handles variable length via an insertion-based mechanism rather than padding, allowing for generation on arbitrary state spaces such as layout and molecule generation.

#ComputerVision #VideoGeneration #DiffusionModels #AIResearch #GenerativeAI

Source: Autoregressive View Model Source: Variable Length Diffuse Everything: Arbitrary Length Generative Modeling on Arbitrary State Spaces

item.title: BFL Releases FLUX 3, Training Models on Video Signals Together
item.description:
BFL Releases FLUX 3, Training Models on Video Signals Together

Intro

BFL released FLUX 3, training a new image generation model on video signals together to improve temporal consistency and understanding of motion.

🧩 Origins

Stable Diffusion’s release prompted Dustin Podell and others to go fulltime into AI. Podell stuck to human content creation while immersing in AI content creation with Andreas Blattmann and Stability AI’s image generation team. After Stability AI fell apart, Anj Midha helped the core group spin out to BFL, which built the FLUX series.

🔍 FLUX 3’s Approach

BFL’s argument for training FLUX 3 was to combine three signals: a still shows where the ball is, a video shows how it got there, and the sound of impact can tell when it hit something even if the camera missed contact. A key example in the FLUX 3 release is the horse in motion.

⚙️ Video Upscaling

FLUX 3 derives its video upscaler from the same FLUX 3 backbone. Sharpening each frame independently might look terrific, but playing it back can show shimmering as the upscaler makes slightly different decisions per frame. Temporal consistency matters even for higher-resolution files. Andreas Blattmann notes that ordinary 2D video contains evidence about what objects look like from other angles.

🚀 Technical Execution

An autoregressive model can learn from all tokens in a training example at once. On the diffusion side, the team distilled long sampling processes down to a handful of steps. Dustin Podell’s early Kontext experiment showed that a model able to draw a dog wearing a hat seemed to know where hats go. A few hours of training got the model to place a logo on a shirt, which was rough but sufficient for offsite discussion. The team then spent months refining the data and model.

💡 Unexpected Use Case

Users fed FLUX old, degraded family photos to restore them, then shared the pictures with families. Podell hadn’t predicted this use. After discussing identity preservation across edits and frames, he noted it’s a nice example of users noticing when something is done right.

#StableDiffusion #AI #FLUX3 #VideoGeneration #ImageGeneration

Source: Building Visual Intelligence — Andreas Blattmann & Dustin Podell, Black Forest Labs — Latent Space

item.title: OpenMontage: First Open‑Source Agentic Video Production System
item.description:
OpenMontage: First Open‑Source Agentic Video Production System

The open‑source community released OpenMontage, described as the world’s first open‑source, agentic video production system.

🔍 Overview

  • World’s first open‑source, agentic video production system.
  • Provides 12 production pipelines, over 100 tools, and more than 700 agent skill and production‑knowledge files.
  • Turns an AI coding assistant into a full video production studio.

🧩 How it works

  • The agent builds a corpus from free stock footage and open archives.
  • It retrieves actual motion clips, edits them into a timeline, and renders a finished piece.
  • OpenMontage can make image‑based videos and also make a real video video for free/open‑source workflows.

⚙️ Key details

  • License: AGPLv3.
  • Website: https://openmontage.video.
  • Follow The Build.

🎬 Showcase productions

Production Length Style / Highlights Cost
SIGNAL FROM TOMORROW — Cinematic sci‑fi trailer; concept, script, scene plan, Veo‑generated motion clips, soundtrack, Remotion composition —
THE LAST BANANA 60 s Pixar‑style animated short; 6 Kling v3‑generated motion clips (via fal.ai), Google Chirp3‑HD narration, royalty‑free piano music, TikTok‑style word‑level captions, Remotion composition $1.33
OBJECTS IN OVERDRIVE 54 s Music‑driven 3D showcase; ten objects with distinct choreography (gravity‑shifting furniture, frozen car drifts, cloth impacts, refractive lenses, moving gears, acrobatic robot, and more); custom Blender animation & physics, kinetic typography, phonk soundtrack; rendered with Blender Eevee/Cycles and assembled with FFmpeg; no narration —
Reimagine Your Universe 50 s Vertical transformation film; five generated motion scenes, sparse Google Chirp narration, Pixabay score, HyperFrames composition linking separate clips into one authored cinematic journey about $4
Products Come to Life 60 s Product film built from approved hero stills; five hard‑surface products separate into their own engineering and reassemble, each still pinned as the first and last frame so the model invents motion without losing product identity; image‑to‑video generation, bespoke sound, narration, custom composition —
Imagine the Possibilities with OpenMontage — Seven generated worlds collected into one music‑only showcase; three image models supply campaign, fashion, and miniature‑world artwork; four video models expand the journey through architecture, material transformation, a living greenhouse, and a creature encounter —

🚀 Availability

OpenMontage is released under the AGPLv3 license and can be accessed at https://openmontage.video.

💡 Why it matters

  • Enables free/open‑source video creation pipelines that combine stock‑footage retrieval, AI‑generated motion clips, and open‑source rendering tools.
  • Demonstrates end‑to‑end production—from concept to final render—at costs as low as $1.33 for a 60‑second short.

#OpenMontage #OpenSource #AIProduction #VideoGeneration

Source: calesthio/OpenMontage

item.title: Dreamina Introduces Seedance 2.5 for Multimodal Video Generation
item.description:
Dreamina Introduces Seedance 2.5 for Multimodal Video Generation

🔍 Overview

Dreamina is positioned as the first pick for creators who want to develop a visual idea and turn it into a video through prompts and references. The new Seedance 2.5 route expands that capability by bringing audio and multiple reference types into the brief.

🧩 How it works

Dreamina’s Seedance 2.5 guide describes a multimodal route:

  • Images can establish appearance.
  • Video can communicate movement.
  • Audio can help direct the sound or performance.

The workflow makes particular sense when you have a visual idea but not yet a finished starting frame. For example, a product reveal may need a particular object, a restrained camera move, and a sound timed to the reveal. In that scenario, a source image settles the composition, a motion reference communicates pacing, and an audio brief identifies what the audience should hear.

⚙️ Capabilities

  • Turn a visual idea into a video through prompts and references.
  • Seedance 2.5 adds native audio and supports multiple reference types.
  • Handles scenarios such as social campaigns, music visuals, or short stories that need characters and settings established before movement is added.
  • Example (Seedance 2.0 Mini): a still photograph and a five‑second setting produce successive frames with changing clouds, reflections, and light while the shoreline, grass, and fence remain recognizable.
  • Light changes across frames; a brief requiring fixed illumination would need a different result.
  • The Mini example does not demonstrate Seedance 2.5 audio or motion continuity.

📊 Comparison with other tools

Tool Notable Feature
Dreamina Multimodal reference‑guided video generation (Seedance 2.5)
Google Veo Strong alternative for audiovisual scene generation; supports native audio; documented approaches to references, scene continuity, and camera direction
Runway Considered for deliberate shot development
Kling Offers more control over reference assets and story beats
Adobe Firefly Supports an Adobe‑centered creative workflow
Luma Helps teams evaluate generation and video editing together
Hailuo with MiniMax H3 Provides multimodal references and native audio

💰 Cost considerations

  • Consult Dreamina’s pricing alongside the cost shown for the selected operation.
  • A free completion under one account offer does not establish the future cost of every model.
  • Reference‑guided animation still reconstructs the scene, so an instruction to preserve a package or face needs visual review.

📅 Availability

Product information was checked October 9–10, 2026.

The comparison covers documented creative controls, access and project fit, with a Dreamina image‑animation example referenced above.

#Dreamina #AIAnimation #MultimodalAI #VideoGeneration

Source: 7 AI Video Generators for Your Next Creative Project

item.title: Sogni Launches Spark Credit System and New Seedance and HappyHorse Models
item.description:
Sogni Launches Spark Credit System and New Seedance and HappyHorse Models

Sogni has introduced a unified credit system called Spark to power its suite of SuperApps, SDK, and creative workflows. Alongside this new payment infrastructure, Sogni has released several upgraded models for image and video generation that require Premium Spark for access.

🧩 How it works

Spark credits function as a universal currency across Sogni services. One Spark is equivalent to the baseline SDXL fast render value, with an internal value pegged at $0.005 USD per unit of GPU inference time. Users can purchase Premium Spark via Stripe for pay-as-you-go access, or prepay using USDC or USDT on Base, Etherlink, or Ethereum at dashboard.sogni.ai.

⚙️ Key details

Premium Spark is required to access premium model gates and external API models. Specific model requirements include:

Model Capabilities Requirements
Seedance 2.0 Mini 480p and 720p resolution Premium Spark
Seedance 2.0 480p, 720p, 1080p, 4K; up to 12 reference assets Premium Spark
Seedance 2.5 480p and 720p; multimodal reference path Premium Spark
HappyHorse 1.1 720p, 1080p; synchronized audio and lip-sync Premium Spark

🚀 Availability

  • Seedance 2.5 supports up to 30 media items per request, including reference images, videos, and audio clips.
  • HappyHorse 1.1 generations range from 3-15 seconds at a fixed 24fps across various aspect ratios, including 16:9, 9:16, and 1:1.
  • The Sogni model gpt-image-2 is restricted to Premium Spark users only.
  • Premium Spark access for Seedance and HappyHorse models includes credit-card premium coverage checks.

#Sogni #AI #GenerativeAI #SparkCredits #VideoGeneration

Source: Pricing Reference | Sogni: Learn

item.title: Beyond Text Prompts: How Google's VEO 3 & FLOW Are Revolutionizing AI Filmmaking
item.description:
🎬 Beyond Text Prompts: How Google’s VEO 3 & FLOW Are Revolutionizing AI Filmmaking

✨ Summary: Discover how Google’s VEO 3 and FLOW are transforming video creation through native audio generation, realistic physics, and intuitive camera controls. This guide explores how these AI tools are putting professional-grade filmmaking capabilities directly into creators’ hands, requiring nothing more than simple text prompts.

🌟 The New Frontier of AI-Generated Video

The world of generative AI has been evolving at breakneck speed, but Google DeepMind’s latest creation might be the most impressive leap yet for creators. VEO 3, working in tandem with the FLOW platform, represents a paradigm shift in how we approach video creation – moving from complex production workflows to simple text-based instructions that generate entire cinematic experiences.

What makes this development particularly groundbreaking isn’t just the quality of the generated videos (though that’s remarkable in itself), but how the system bridges the gap between imagination and execution with unprecedented ease.

📸 Check out the FLOW interface overview showing the intuitive project layout and generation options.

🧠 Understanding VEO 3: Google DeepMind’s Video Powerhouse

VEO 3 is not just another incremental improvement in the AI video generation space – it represents a fundamental rethinking of what’s possible. Unlike previous models that generated silent video requiring separate audio processing, VEO 3 delivers something revolutionary: 𝗻𝗮𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗶𝗼 𝗴𝗲𝗻𝗲𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻.

This means that from a single prompt, the system can create:

  • Perfectly synchronized dialogue
  • Environmental sound effects
  • Ambient background music
  • Realistic sound mixing

The realism factor is perhaps what sets VEO 3 apart most dramatically. The model demonstrates a sophisticated understanding of physics, with objects and characters moving naturally within generated environments. Characters speak with lip movements that sync convincingly to dialogue, and scenes flow with a cinematic quality that previously required extensive human direction.

For example, a prompt describing “a busy subway car with commuters during rush hour” would generate not only the visual scene but also the rumbling of the train, the murmur of conversations, and the ambient sounds of a crowded subway – all perfectly synchronized and spatially accurate.

🔊 Imagine hearing authentic audio that matches perfectly with generated visuals – no separate processing required.

🎭 FLOW: The Filmmaker’s New Canvas

While VEO 3 handles the heavy computational lifting, Google’s FLOW platform provides the creative interface that makes the technology accessible and useful. Think of FLOW as a comprehensive AI filmmaking studio designed specifically to harness VEO 3’s capabilities alongside other Google AI models like Gemini (for language processing) and Imagen (for image generation).

𝗞𝗲𝘆 𝗙𝗲𝗮𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲𝘀 𝗼𝗳 𝗙𝗟𝗢𝗪:

  1. 𝙏𝙝𝙚 𝙋𝙧𝙤𝙢𝙥𝙩 𝘽𝙤𝙭 🎯 FLOW starts with natural language instructions. Users can switch between different generation modes through a drop-down menu, selecting text-to-video, frames-to-video, or ingredients-to-video options depending on their creative needs.

  2. 𝘾𝙖𝙢𝙚𝙧𝙖 𝘾𝙤𝙣𝙩𝙧𝙤𝙡𝙨 🎥 Perhaps one of the most exciting features is the ability to specify camera movements and angles. Want a slow pan across a sunset beach? A dramatic dolly zoom on a character’s revelation? Simply select from camera icons and add specific movements, with the ability to preview camera paths before generation.

  3. 𝙎𝙘𝙚𝙣𝙚 𝘽𝙪𝙞𝙡𝙙𝙚𝙧 🏗️ This tool transforms FLOW from a mere clip generator to a true filmmaking platform. Users can assemble longer sequences by arranging and connecting clips, trim with handle controls, and even use the “Jump To” feature that leverages Gemini AI to generate subsequent clips that maintain narrative continuity.

  4. 𝗔𝘀𝘀𝗲𝘁 𝗠𝗮𝗻𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 📦 The “Ingredients” drawer is where FLOW truly shines for professional workflows. Users can save and reuse visual elements across different scenes – ensuring character consistency, location continuity, and visual coherence throughout a project.

📸 The Scene Builder interface showing how clips can be arranged, trimmed and extended to create longer sequences.

🚀 Workflow Deep Dive: Creating with VEO 3 & FLOW

Let’s walk through the typical creative process using these tools:

1. Project Initiation

Users begin in the Project View, where they can scroll through existing projects or start fresh. The interface is designed for quick access to all video projects and their various generations.

2. Generation Approach

Depending on your starting point, you might choose:

  • Text-to-Video: Start with just a written description
  • Frames-to-Video: Begin with first/last frames (uploaded or generated)
  • Ingredients-to-Video: Combine multiple visual elements into a cohesive scene

3. Enhancement & Direction

Once your base generation is complete, you can refine it with:

  • Camera controls for specific movements
  • Extended clip length using the “Extend” feature
  • Trimming for precise timing

4. Scene Construction

The real magic happens in the Scene Builder, where you can:

  • Arrange clips in sequence
  • Use “Jump To” for AI-assisted continuity between clips
  • Save specific frames as ingredients for later use

5. Final Output

When satisfied with your scene, you can download the completed video with its synchronized audio track – ready for use in larger projects or direct publishing.

🎞️ Your downloaded scenes include perfectly synchronized audio without requiring separate processing.

💭 The Future of Filmmaking: Democratized Creativity

What makes the VEO 3 and FLOW combination truly revolutionary is how it democratizes filmmaking. Creative vision becomes the primary currency, rather than technical skill or production budget. A filmmaker with a clear concept but limited resources can now generate scenes that would have previously required expensive equipment, locations, and post-production work.

This isn’t about replacing traditional filmmaking – it’s about expanding who gets to be a filmmaker. FLOW provides a framework that still requires creative direction, storytelling skill, and artistic vision. The difference is that the technical barriers have been dramatically lowered.

As these tools continue to evolve, we’ll likely see entirely new forms of creative expression emerge – hybrid workflows where AI-generated content works alongside traditional footage, or entirely new genres built around the unique capabilities of models like VEO 3.

The question isn’t whether AI will change filmmaking, but how creators will harness these tools to tell stories that weren’t possible before. What kinds of films might emerge when the constraints of physical production no longer apply?
